author: Joe Mullin
description:
Software patents are mostly vague, hard to define, and widely abused. Most tech patent lawsuits aren’t filed by companies that make real products. They’re filed by patent trolls, companies that acquire patents to extract payments through litigation and legal threats. 

A patent on one feature of a smartphone shouldn’t give the patent owner the power to threaten the existence of the entire product line. But that is exactly the leverage patent trolls want—and the current administration is helping them to get it. 

In two recent patent cases, Radian Memory Systems v. Samsung and Collision Communications v. Samsung, the Justice Department and the U.S. Patent and Trademark Offic
title: The Justice Department Wants To Give Patent Trolls More Power

author: Katharine Trendacosta
description: There are all sorts of reasons to be against the merger of Paramount and Warner Brothers-Discovery. There's the obvious problem of increasing concentration in the already pretty-concentrated film and TV industry. People have problems with Paramount's owner Skydance interfering  with its news coverage and late night comedy. But one of the biggest is the way we are losing choice and access to information and culture.
title: The Paramount-Warner Brothers Deal Could Usher in Another Age of Lost Media

author: Karen Gullo
description:
EFF and 27 other human rights organizations today called on the European Commission to retract a dangerous proposal granting its border agency Frontex to request that national authorities issue take-down orders for social media content and giving it so-called “trusted flagger” status under the Digital Services Act (DSA), the EU regulation governing online platforms and content moderation in the region.

title: European Commission Plan to Give Frontex Trusted Flagger Status Is A Threat to Free Speech
